candidate_relations.rationale: The storage-verification runtime implements the read-only PEMS/COVE, schema, deterministic-decoding, and receipt checks required by the R14 storage-verification contract.
The storage-verification tests exercise the runtime against valid state and multiple malformed canonical states, strengthening the runtime behavior claim.
The accepted immutable local-package distribution model is compatible with and supports the requirement that installed runtime remain usable without source-repository or network fallback.

The adversarial Rupi tests demonstrate that contextual language, repository state, readiness labels, and legacy utilities do not create protected authority, strengthening the lifecycle-agent authority boundary.
The Rupi design contract keeps project bootstrap distinct from operator, Steward, canonical, and admission work, strengthening the bootstrap contract exclusion boundary.
The primitive-inventory tests verify one governing primitive per Rupi action and reject legacy Steward setup as an authority route, strengthening the Rupi composition-only contract.
The admission executor deterministically normalizes and validates PEMS and performs COVE encoding/round-trip logic, supplying the canonical artifacts later checked by R14 storage verification.
The activation runtime depends on durable role and Steward-authorization state maintained by the role runtime rather than treating activation evidence as self-authorizing.
The package validator enforces safe normalized relative paths and managed-root containment, strengthening the accepted install-package path-safety requirements.
The install/bootstrap handoff tests exercise the composed install-status-bootstrap-status lifecycle and its authority stop, strengthening the Rupi lifecycle-adapter behavior claim.
The adversarial Rupi tests show role names and contextual signals cannot manufacture Steward or admission authority, strengthening the role-registry no-authority-from-membership rule.
The Rupi handoff tests verify bootstrap and lifecycle failures do not advance into protected authority work, strengthening the lifecycle-agent primitive-boundary contract.

The grant-operation tests verify operation-specific grantor capability and immutable issuance evidence, strengthening the authority-grant tests covering immutable definitions and non-delegable failure behavior.
The role-registry contract explicitly prevents registry membership from granting protected authority, strengthening bootstrap's exclusion of role-authority creation.

The Steward handoff specification forbids contextual substitutes for explicit Steward authority, strengthening the Rupi primitive-inventory test requirement that legacy setup cannot serve as an alternate authority route.
The bootstrap contract explicitly creates no role authority or Steward state, strengthening the role-registry distinction between role availability and authorization.
The role runtime supplies and separates the durable role-registration and Steward-authorization states that activation evidence must validate for an exact invocation.
The role-registry contract separates registration from Steward authorization, strengthening the runtime implementation claim that these states are distinct.

The activation-evidence contract requires current role availability and Steward assignment for one exact invocation, strengthening adversarial evidence that contextual signals cannot manufacture authority.
The grant-operation tests exercise operation-specific grantor capability, strengthening the runtime requirement for explicit operation classes and bounded scope targets.
